name: Rites of the Earthmother
summary: At Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind sends you beyond Red Cloud Mesa to continue the Rites of the Earthmother. After the first trials, you carry a carved totem north to Bloodhoof Village and Baine Bloodhoof.

sections.title: Leaving the Mesa
sections.body: Young tauren have tested their strength at Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa for generations. The first trials teach discipline and resolve. Yet the sacred Rites of the Earthmother reach beyond surviving the mesa's wildlife. Chief Hawkwind knows when an initiate is ready to leave the sheltered hunting grounds and join the wider community.

sections.title: A Token for Baine
sections.body: Chief Hawkwind gives you a hand-carved totem to introduce you on the road from Narache to the central settlements. Carry it down the winding path to Bloodhoof Village and present yourself to Baine Bloodhoof, the young chieftain and son of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof. The totem is your credential and seal of approval. It marks your readiness for the rites of spirit and wisdom ahead.

faq.q: What is the purpose of this quest?
aliases: why do rites of the earthmother
faq.answer: The rites carry you from Camp Narache into the wider tauren community at Bloodhoof Village, where the next trials begin.
Baine Bloodhoof is the son of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof and the young chieftain of Bloodhoof Village. He oversees the spiritual and martial testing of young tauren.

faq.q: What is the Totem of Hawkwind?
faq.answer: The Totem of Hawkwind is a wooden token hand-carved by Chief Hawkwind of Camp Narache. It is an official credential and seal of approval, showing Baine Bloodhoof that you have Hawkwind's blessing to undertake further rites.
In Bloodhoof Village, Baine sets you on the Rite of Vision. It tests your spiritual attunement through sacred ancestral visions.
Bloodhoof Village lies north of Camp Narache, along the shores of Stonebull Lake in central Mulgore. Follow the main road down from the mesa and head north.

faq.q: Why must the Earthmother rites be completed?
faq.answer: The Rites of the Earthmother are sacred tauren traditions. Passing their stages shows physical fortitude, spiritual connection, and wisdom, earning recognition from the elders of Thunder Bluff.

angles.text: As a young tauren, you walk the path of the Earthmother to prove your worth to the elders and find your place among the united tribes.
As a member of the Horde, you take part in traditions that strengthen tribal unity across Mulgore and prepare new defenders with warrior prowess and spiritual grounding.
